subject: Coordination: demo time window for APAC (Tokyo / Singapore / Sydney) — ICS conversion check
messages:
From: Aoi Tanaka <aoi.tanaka@brightgrid.co.jp>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 00:45:00 +0900
Subject: Quick demo request — APAC availability this week

Hi Ben,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. We're ready to see Redwood running with our sample storefront traffic. We're based in Tokyo but have engineers in Singapore and Sydney who want to join for a single walkthrough (approx 45 minutes).

Could you propose 2–3 slots that work for your APAC team? Ideal window for BrightGrid: 10:00–16:00 JST but Singapore is -1 hour and Sydney is +1/+2 depending on DST. Apologies — I know the next-day labels can be tricky when invites cross midnight.

Best,
Aoi
Aoi Tanaka | Product Lead, BrightGrid
Attachments: none
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Aoi Tanaka <aoi.tanaka@brightgrid.co.jp>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 02:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Quick demo request — APAC availability this week

Hi Aoi — thanks, sounds good.

We can do the following slots (local times shown in parentheses):
- Option A: 2026-09-16 14:00 JST (13:00 SGT / 15:00 AEST)
- Option B: 2026-09-16 16:30 JST (15:30 SGT / 17:30 AEST)
- Option C: 2026-09-17 09:00 JST (08:00 SGT / 10:00 AEST)

Two quick notes: 1) Sydney switches to DST on 2026-10-04 but all dates above are in September so AEST applies; 2) some calendar clients will show the meeting on a different local date if you invite across 00:00 UTC — happy to send UTC times if that's easier.

Vivek, Priyom — can one of you join Option A or B from the platform side? We'll include a short perf section for Tokyo-local inference and a note about Dedicated vs Hosted routing.

Aoi — attaching a short demo pack and a draft .ics I can send once you confirm a slot. If everyone prefers a single UTC anchor: Option A = 2026-09-16 05:00 UTC.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter | Senior Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-demo-pack.pdf, proposed-ics.ics
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 03:20:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Quick demo request — APAC availability this week

Ben — I can cover Option A (14:00 JST) and do the short latency section. Priyom — can you cover any security/compliance questions?

Also: Ben, when we send the .ics, make sure DTSTART/DTEND are set with UTC offsets (e.g., 20260916T050000Z) — we've had Exchange clients render the date a day earlier if the timezone header is ambiguous.

Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni | Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Samuel Lim <s.samuel@cloudbazaar.sg>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aoi Tanaka <aoi.tanaka@brightgrid.co.jp>, Claire O'Neill <claire@retailco.au>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 09:05:00 +0800
Subject: Re: Quick demo request — APAC availability this week

Hi Ben / Aoi — thanks for the options. Quick clarification from our side: when I accepted the Calendly invite it showed "Thu, Sep 16, 11:00 PM" in my Outlook (SGT), which seemed like the next-day label compared to the JST times you listed. We're worried that some participants (Sydney) might see the meeting on Sep 17 locally because of calendar conversion.

Could you please resend the confirmed time as: 1) UTC timestamp and 2) each local time label (JST / SGT / AEST) so we can paste into local calendars? That avoids confusion if someone's client is set to 12-hour clock vs 24-hour or different DST rules.

Also — can you include the raw .ics as an attachment (not a link)? Some corporate calendars block external calendar links.

Samuel
Samuel Lim | IT Lead, CloudBazaar (SG)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Aoi Tanaka <aoi.tanaka@brightgrid.co.jp>, Samuel Lim <s.samuel@cloudbazaar.sg>, Claire O'Neill <claire@retailco.au>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 09:38:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Quick demo request — confirmed time and ICS (UTC + local labels)

Thanks, Samuel — good catch. Finalizing for clarity:
CONFIRMED: Option A selected by majority
- UTC: 2026-09-16 05:00–05:45 UTC
- JST: 2026-09-16 14:00–14:45 JST (Tokyo)
- SGT: 2026-09-16 13:00–13:45 SGT (Singapore)
- AEST: 2026-09-16 15:00–15:45 AEST (Sydney)

I've attached the raw .ics (proposed-ics.ics) and the demo pack PDF. Notes: 1) the .ics uses absolute UTC times (DTSTART:20260916T050000Z / DTEND:20260916T054500Z); 2) if anyone's calendar still shows Sep 17, reply-all with a screenshot and we'll reissue the invite as an explicit UTC-only invite.

Agenda: 5m intros / 25m walkthrough (latency + routing) / 10m Q&A.

See you there — will send a reminder 1 hour prior.

Best,
Ben
Attachments: proposed-ics.ics, redwood-demo-pack.pdf
